issues.detail: The Greek 'δοκιμαζειν' (dokimazein) in this context means 'to test/examine/evaluate' the times, but the Vietnamese 'thử nghiệm' usually refers to a physical experiment or trial. More importantly, the Greek 'τις δοκιμαζειν' (how do you test) is rendered as a question about why they are *not* testing it ('sao... không thử nghiệm'), whereas the Greek asks 'how' (πως) they are testing it.
The Greek 'τις δοκιμαζειν' implies a question of manner/method ('how'), but the Vietnamese 'sao... không' translates to 'why not', changing the nature of the rhetorical question.
